claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a lamellar dual-phase microstructure.
The initial lamellar microstructure of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is coarse.
Cryogenic rolling followed by annealing refines the eutectic lamellae into an ultrafine-grained duplex structure.
Cryogenic rolling followed by annealing increases the density of phase boundaries and grain boundaries.
Increased grain-boundary density strengthens the alloy by hindering dislocation motion.
The duplex microstructure improves strain partitioning between phases and thereby improves ductility.
Combining a soft FCC phase with a hard BCC phase or intermetallic phase can balance strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Cryo-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has greater strength than cold-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Cryo-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has greater ductility than cold-rolled and annealed AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Cryo-rolling and annealing can increase yield strength by approximately 20-30% relative to cold-rolling and annealing.
Cryo-rolling and annealing can improve elongation by a few percentage points relative to cold-rolling and annealing.
The simultaneous strength and ductility improvement holds under quasi-static tensile loading at room temperature.
An annealing temperature can be optimized to induce refinement without causing coarsening.
The proposed effect should extend to eutectic high-entropy alloys with lamellar compositions and phase distributions similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Changes in alloy composition or processing parameters may limit the simultaneous strength and ductility improvement.
